title: The Dungeon Dive Update - June 2021
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fHYBRGdrXo0

Daniel (@dungeondive) explains a quiet stretch on the channel, and the explanation is unusually unguarded.

The day job has been busier than it has ever been, to the point where evenings go to the television, a video game or a book because there is nothing left over for anything more demanding. Several large games have been sitting set up on the table for weeks, unplayed, because he cannot muster the energy to learn them. A jury duty summons lands the following week, which could mean days sitting indoors in a courthouse in an area with low vaccination uptake, followed by job work at night. He also wants to get back to an office: working out of his hobby room has collapsed the separation between the place he goes to escape stress and the place the stress happens, and he can feel what it is doing to him.

Out of that comes a pivot that shaped a good deal of what followed. What he finds himself drawn to now are games with few components and light rules — Four Against Darkness and d100 Dungeon. He sets out a plan to build a party, work through the supplements towards Breachers of the Bone Belfry, and asks whether the fan-made overland hexcrawl expansion is worth the effort.

----

Burnout pushed Daniel towards games with fewer moving parts rather than away from games altogether. When your capacity drops, which way do you go?
